_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the envelope's mutation vocabulary, its catalog, its committed JSON-carrier vectors, and the third-party reference that reads them. `s.stdio.semio` is the semio ENVELOPE — a union over eighteen semio-native subsets — and its JSON carrier is published schema-first beside the schema types, so a JSON implementation that has never seen this repository can read it and route it by the envelope's own law.

engine.implementation: json Rust crate (maciejhirsz/json-rust) reading the committed envelope carrier

oracles.rationale: 📖️ READS the envelope's committed JSON carrier and ROUTES it by the envelope's published law; `../🔮️oracles/🦀️.rs` is the whole reference. `setSnapshot` replaces the envelope with its payload; a wrapped arm mutation whose tag matches the envelope's `subset` reaches that arm and lands on the arm's own committed result, produced by that arm's registered independent implementation (see each `apply-<arm>-applied` fixture's generator) and never by this repository's Rust; a mismatched arm is refused with `mutation.target-missing`; every inverse restores the envelope it started from. The subject reads the same files only through the schema-derived bridge (`decode_semio_snapshot_json`/`encode_semio_snapshot_json`/`decode_semio_mutation_json`, first-party `pack` JSON over the schema types' own `ToValue`/`FromValue`), so the comparison is between two JSON implementations that share no code. json-rust, not `serde_json`: `serde_json` is a production dependency of the subject crate itself, and `🧾️json`'s own oracle records why a reference the implementation already links is no independent evidence; json-rust appears nowhere in the production graph and is already linked by this plugin's oracle crate, so no dependency is added. Honest limit: the carrier cannot say what a delegated arm verb DOES to its arm — that answer is the arm's own independent implementation's committed result, which this reader reads rather than recomputes.

engine.implementation: Ajv 8 JSON Schema validator over the platform JSON.parse

probes.rationale: 🔬️ The SECOND, independent implementation of the envelope and of every arm verb its vectors exercise, in another language and on another engine family than the json-rust oracle the parity case runs: the platform `JSON.parse` reads every vector this subset registers, Ajv 8 holds each document to the carrier the subset publishes (`../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json`, `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🔣️.json` and every schema they reference), and the envelope law plus each arm verb are applied in TypeScript written from the arms' published leaf schemas, sharing no code with the Rust subject or the oracle. Every vector is REPRODUCED from before + mutation and compared with the committed after.

qualification.evidence: Run over all 22 registered vectors: 22/22 conform to the published carrier schemas (after the six arm-schema drifts were fixed at their schemas), 22/22 are reproduced exactly from before + mutation — three set-snapshot, one refusal and the eighteen delegated arm verbs — and a one-character tamper of a committed after-envelope fails exactly that vector.

criteria.detail: 22/22 vectors reproduced from before + mutation: the envelope law for set-snapshot and refusal, the arm's own verb for the eighteen delegated vectors.
canonical comparison is exact: any differing member or array order fails
platform JSON.parse + Ajv; imports nothing of the Rust crate or the json-rust oracle
reads committed files only; no clock, no network
ajv 8.20.0 resolves from the repository's root node_modules

comparisonPipelines.description: Carrier-level reproduction of every vector by a second, independent implementation: the platform JSON.parse + Ajv 8 holds before, mutation and after to the published carrier schemas, and the envelope law plus the arm verb applied in TypeScript must land on the committed after.

stages.description: Every registered vector conforms, and every vector is reproduced exactly from before + mutation.
